skill_traces.query:
John: Hey Tim! Long time no talk - a lot has been going on since then!
Tim: Hey John! Long time no see! Can't wait to catch up and hear all about what you've been up to.
John: Seems like forever since we caught up! I'm now mentoring the younger players on my team. It's super rewarding and I'm loving sharing my skills and knowledge with them. It's also a great way for me to stay involved in the game during the off-season.
Tim: Wow! Mentoring must be so rewarding. You get to show others what you know - that's awesome! Is it difficult? Any hiccups?
John: There are challenges, since everyone is so different. But it's been awesome gaining experience and adapting, motivating and encouraging everyone. It's been great to watch each of them develop and reach their goals - such a reward!
Tim: Wow, that's awesome! It must be really rewarding to see them reach their goals. What's it like mentoring them?
John: Mentoring them has been awesome! Seeing their growth, improvement, and confidence is so fulfilling. I'm glad I could make a positive impact on their lives. Here's a pic of me and some of the younger players at a recent practice.
Tim: You're really doing great with them. Do any of them see you as a mentor?
John: Some of them do see me as a mentor, which is really rewarding. I try to provide them with advice and support on and off the court. Being a positive role model for them is something I enjoy.
Tim: That's incredible! How does it feel to have their trust and admiration? It must be such an honor to be a positive role model for them.
John: It feels great to have their trust and admiration. Being a role model for these young athletes is so fulfilling. I'm glad my experiences can help shape their future and inspire them to go after their dreams.
Tim: You're doing a great job with them. Way to go! This is what I've been up to.
John: Wow, stunning! And thanks. Really appreciate it. Means a lot.
Tim: I took this pic last summer. Seeing it was so stunning. Thanks for appreciating it. It means a lot to me.
John: Where did you capture this? Nature is truly amazing, isn't it?
Tim: I snapped that pic on my trip to the Smoky Mountains last year. It was incredible seeing it in person. Nature's really something else!
John: Yeah, it's amazing how nature's beauty and grandeur can take our breath away. It's so nice to escape the noise of the city and relax in nature. Good for you to get to enjoy that stunning view!
Tim: Nature is indeed refreshing. A good break from school.
John: How are you doing in shcool?
Tim: Doing good! Busy with studies but finding time to relax with books - good balance.
John: Cool! Finding that balance is key. Are you currently reading any books?
Tim: I'm reading this book and I'm totally hooked! What about you?
John: I haven't had much time to read, but after we talked I finally picked up a book and it's been awesome! Talk to you later!

selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.

These statements directly trigger the photo-sharing extraction procedure.

content: During extraction, if the source states that someone helped another person achieve a specific goal or outcome, record that outcome explicitly in the memory content.
Do not replace named outcomes with a general paraphrase; include both the general description and the explicit achievement.
Keep the memory evidence-bound by using the speaker's concrete wording for what was achieved.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.
